canonicalSubStages.label: Portal/account registration and Unit creation on a single-window EODB-type portal, prior to filing the service-specific application
Online submission of the Factory Licence application
Upload/submission of supporting documents (forms, plans, certificates, NOCs, etc.)
Payment of the statutory/prescribed Factory Licence fee
A separate antecedent approval (Building Plan/Factory Drawing Approval, or plan/stability-certificate acceptance) bundled into or preceding the same Factory Licence flow
Departmental review/verification of the submitted application and documents
Department flags missing/incorrect documents or raises a query/objection/show-cause notice to the applicant
Applicant corrects, clarifies, or resubmits in response to a deficiency/query/objection
File forwarded/routed between offices or officials with no independently described review or decision content
Physical/site/field verification of the factory premises
Tests, certifications or sign-offs obtained from empanelled third-party agencies/auditors as an explicit step in the licensing flow
Decision by the competent authority to approve/grant/sanction the Factory Licence
Generation, delivery, or download of the Factory Licence certificate
A periodic renewal requirement described as part of or adjoining the Factory Licence flow

notes: Delhi (DL) is the thinnest record in the dataset: its FGD-only reconstruction has only 2 raw steps ('Apply for Factory License' and 'Inspection(s)'), with no explicit scrutiny, fee-payment, approval or issuance step described by participants, so its canonicalSubStageCount of 2 almost certainly understates DL's real process rather than reflecting an unusually lean one; its ED dataset currently has no Factory License entry to cross-check against.

Punjab (PB) is similarly thin for a 4-step record: participants described application, manual file movement, uncoordinated parallel department requirements, and an eventual approval, but no explicit document-upload, fee-payment, inspection or certificate-issuance step, so its canonicalSubStageCount of 4 should be read as a floor, not a precise count.

Madhya Pradesh (MP) self-flagged in its own source record as 'a comparatively short, thinner session (five participants, 40 minutes)'; its mapping is accordingly treated with extra caution and several low-confidence flags (document upload, inspection, and inferred approval).

ANTECEDENT_APPROVAL (a bundled Building Plan/Factory Drawing Approval, or an equivalent plan/stability-certificate acceptance) was only included where a state's actual step text describes it as part of or a precondition to the same Factory Licence flow (HP, AP, CG, DNHDD, AS; lower-confidence for JK, whose text makes it explicitly conditional, and KL, whose step is private plan-preparation rather than a department approval). It was deliberately NOT added for states where a stability or building-plan certificate appears only in a documents list but not in any step text (e.g. MN, UP), per the instruction not to invent a sub-stage from a document checklist alone.

THIRD_PARTY_CERTIFICATION (tests/sign-offs from empanelled agencies or auditors) is supported by only two states' explicit step text (GJ's stability/air-compressor/lift testing step, MH's Consent-to-Operate/safety-audit/HIRA compilation step). It was not extended to other states that merely list a stability certificate as a required document without describing the certification process as a step.

Many states' terminal step uses only the word 'issued' or 'granted' without separately using 'approve/approval' anywhere in the record (TG, WB, AP, AS, HR, MH's provisional-licence step, MP). In each such case APPROVAL was still mapped, since issuance necessarily implies an approval decision was taken, but every one of these mappings was explicitly flagged confidence:low with a stated reason, rather than treated as directly evidenced the way RJ, HP, JH, MN, CG, DNHDD, PY and UP's explicit 'approved/issued' or 'approves...issues' wording was.

Two 'scrutiny'-tagged steps were never treated as automatically equivalent just because both carry a scrutiny-type phase. For example, AP's 'Deviations handled if found' step is about handling deviations from an already-approved building plan after inspection, not generic document scrutiny, and was mapped to DEFICIENCY_NOTICE/RESUBMISSION at low confidence (functional analogy) rather than high confidence, since the described activity differs from a typical document-completeness check.

Steps whose text contains no independently described review or decision content beyond moving a file between offices (JH's 'Forwarding'/'Recommendation', PY's two JCF/CAF forwarding steps, AP's category-based routing, MN's inspection referral) were kept as a distinct INTERNAL_ROUTING sub-stage rather than folded into SCRUTINY or APPROVAL, since the source text does not describe any review or decision activity at those specific steps.
